scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF from
each other!! From it_hod, the department head's machine, none of the CS
computers on 192.168.2.x answer any more -- our own department is fine, it's
just CS that's gone. Something around the router that joins the two
departments must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and
rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Cross-department L3 connectivity between the IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS (192.168.2.0/24) networks is currently healthy. From the IT HOD host (it_hod 192.168.1.2), ICMP to multiple CS hosts succeeds with 0% loss (e.g., it_hod → cs_lab1 192.168.2.3, cs_lab2 .4, cs_lab3 .5, cs_lab4 .6, cs_hod .2 all replied). Return tests from CS to IT also succeed. The observed TTL=63 on replies confirms a single routed hop, consistent with inter-subnet routing via router0.

Router0 is correctly configured and operating as the L3 gateway for both subnets: eth0=192.168.1.1/24 (IT) and eth1=192.168.2.1/24 (CS). Hosts point to the proper default gateways (it_hod via 192.168.1.1; cs_hod via 192.168.2.1). Router0’s routing table shows directly connected routes for 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and no policy appears to block traffic between them.

Mechanism: If there had been an outage, loss between subnets would present as ICMP timeouts; however, current tests show end-to-end reachability across the router. Localization: router0 eth0/eth1 paths are passing traffic normally.

Root cause: Not reproducible—no misconfiguration or device fault is present at this time.

Corrective fix: None required. If the issue reappears, capture traceroute from a failing IT host to a CS target and check router0 eth0/eth1 link status/ARP tables at that moment to pinpoint any transient L2/host issues.
